ideas.title: Bellows and green rock: smelting the first copper bead
same_form: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: Hot material running through blackbody colours in a close fixed view is what the glass-blowing posts already showed, and a bead appearing in a crucible can easily be a threshold switch, not a reduction. The strong part is the bellows rhythm: the player's timing traded against charcoal use is a real skill loop, and this is the road step everything else waits on.

ideas.title: The hot wire: Joule heat that sets the grass on fire
ideas.critique: A glowing wire alone would be one more glow study. A general fire that any fuel carries, spreading cell by cell and tilted by wind, is something the island has never had, and it gives the friends a danger they actually react to. Its weak spot is the meadow grid: if it is a flat burn texture creeping over the ground rather than heat that real props pick up, it shrinks to a one-off effect.

ideas.title: Plating a friend: copper on Pinchy's claw
ideas.nearest: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: A material that changes by what happened to it, read straight by the path tracer, is a fresh way of showing off materials, and Pinchy volunteering is a nice touch. But Faraday's law with a fitted brine resistance is a single-formula rig, and slowly dipping things in a bowl is a slow toy that is mostly something to look at.

ideas.title: Drawing wire through a die plate
ideas.nearest: A copper wire keeps its bends
same_form: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: This is the same copper rod on a bench, worked again and filmed close; work hardening and annealing are a real step, but the film reads as 'wire changes under a tool' a second time. Pulling without snapping is a skill, though a narrow one.

ideas.title: Brine cells you stack until it bites
ideas.nearest: A wire that spins by itself
ideas.critique: A general nodal solver over what touches what is the backbone of the big goal, and electrode potentials per metal pair give the player real discoveries to make. The shock gag carries the film, but a crest springing to a threshold voltage is close to a scripted reaction; it only lands if the response really grows with the number.

ideas.title: A telegraph from the cottage to the pier
ideas.critique: Two creatures talking over a wire is the most social idea in the round, and a cut between two places is a new shape for a film. The physics is thin, though: a buzzer and a line resistance, while tap patterns mapped onto words that already exist are a lookup table, not something emerging.

ideas.title: A hydrogen lantern from brine
ideas.critique: Night lanterns rising are pretty but expected, and the honest gas yield from one beach cell would take an absurdly long time to lift a paper bag, so either the numbers get bent or nothing lifts. Its link to the road is only that it reuses brine and a cell.

ideas.title: A stone chimney that draws
ideas.critique: Building a structure from toppling parts, with smoke you can read, is a satisfying thing to play with, and the stack effect is a legitimate law. But smoke particles riding a single draft number per chimney is a thin rig, and the payoff (smoke going straight up) is a small one.

ideas.title: Amber and fur: static that chases
ideas.critique: Light things leaping to a stone because of an invisible field is the payoff the island has posted five times this stretch, with charge in place of magnetism. Pickles' fur standing on end and the spark at dusk are the only new things, and the rest is a well-worn recipe.

ideas.title: The materials table every system reads
same_form: A wire that spins by itself
ideas.critique: This is foundation work the road needs, but as data it is invisible, and the pitched film of three variants side by side under a fixed camera is exactly the form the island keeps repeating. It only surprises if what the table makes possible shows up somewhere nobody wired it to.
